title: Horizon Reserve Portfolio: Surge Credits, Predictive Autoscale Buydowns & SLA Lanes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: Enterprise customers want predictable committed spend for Dedicated GPU capacity but also need the ability to handle short, high-throughput events (surges) and smooth cost exposure across bursts. Current reserved offerings are rigid (long commits or manual burst add-ons) and do not map cleanly to seasonal workloads. This ticket defines an experiment and packaging candidate — the Horizon Reserve Portfolio — which bundles: (1) baseline reserved GPU capacity with graduated commitment bands, (2) a denominated pool of 'surge credits' that auto-consume for short bursts across regions, and (3) optional 'predictive autoscale buydowns' that convert short-term overage consumption into discounted reserved capacity if sustained. The design also introduces SLA Lanes (Standard / Priority / Mission-Critical) to align latency/availability with price and capacity routing policies.
acceptance_criteria: A PRD exists describing pricing math, purchase flows, and billing UX mapped to Console and Invoicing
Experiment package includes: commitment band tiers (bronze/silver/gold), surge credit denomination and decay rules, and autoscale buydown thresholds
Legal/SSO/KMS checklist updated and security review completed
Top 10 enterprise customers validated willingness-to-pay via interviews and 3 signed LOIs for pilot
Billing prototype implemented in Console sandbox and usage simulation matches expected revenue curves within 10%

2026-03-08 - Finance feedback (K. Ortega): proposed price anchor: 12-month commit priced at 0.72x on-demand unit, surge credits sold in 100-hour bundles with 12-month expiration. Requesting elasticity sensitivity analysis.

2026-03-10 - Security review kickoff (S. Mehta): identified KMS integration for surge credit audit trail and requirement for immutable usage logs for billing disputes. Set security_review_required=true.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: selling surge credits as prepaid versus pay-after-use (prepaid simplifies revenue recognition; pay-after-use aligns with usage but increases billing ops).

Open question: Should buydown conversion convert consumed surge credits into reserved capacity retroactively or only apply forward-looking discounts? Engineering prefers forward-only to keep accounting simple.

PM rationale for SLA Lanes: isolates priority routing and gives enterprise customers a clear latency/availability product they can buy against, enabling conservative capacity planning for the Priority lane.
Pilot plan: target 3 customers with predictable daily baselines + seasonal spikes (gaming backend, ad-serving partner, and enterprise search with nightly reindex jobs).
review_feedback: Design (Elena Morgan): Console UX needs a visual for active surge credit burn rate and an estimate of 'time-to-exhaust' given current traffic.
Sales (R. Kim): ask pilot customers for preferred surge-credit denominations (hours vs vGPU-minutes). Early indicators favor vGPU-minute bundles for more precise usage mapping.
Legal (D. Novak): require explicit expiration clause, dispute window (60 days), and sample language for refunding unused surge credits on contract termination.

risks: Accounting complexity if surge credits are refundable or transferable between regions
Potential cannibalization of existing reserved SKUs if pricing bands not sufficiently differentiated
Implementation risk: invoice and ledger changes may require billing blackout window or migration plan
Customer confusion if UX does not clearly show how surge credits relate to autoscale and reserved capacity
